subject: Intermittent production latency & error surge — urgent investigation
messages:
From: Sam Irwin <sam@suncrest-commerce.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency and 5xx spike — API errors affecting checkout

Hi Rishi / Monica,

We're seeing a sudden production regression starting ~07:50 PST this morning. Our checkout calls to Redwood's inference API are returning 5xx at ~6-8% and p95 latencies jump from ~200ms to 1.1s for multiple endpoints. Throughput appears reduced — concurrent request queueing increases, and a number of user checkout attempts time out.

Sample request IDs from our logs: req_20261113_0753_az1, req_20261113_0756_kb4, req_20261113_0759_pq2. Happening across two regions (us-west and us-east) but the error modes look similar.

We urgently need a triage and an estimate for when this will be resolved — this is affecting a subset of live traffic and impacting revenue. We're ready to provide PCAPs, flow logs, and any request traces you need.

Please advise next steps.

— Sam
Head of Site Reliability
Suncrest Commerce
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Irwin <sam@suncrest-commerce.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:22:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — API errors affecting checkout

Sam — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption.

We have assigned SRE to lead triage (cc: Grace). Can you please upload a short PCAP (30s around the spike) and a sample of one successful and one failed request trace (the request IDs you pasted are perfect)? That will let us correlate TCP resets and DNS answers. Also confirm whether your traffic is going via our VPC peering or using a public egress to Redwood (I believe Suncrest is peered to our us-west cluster but want to confirm).

Immediate plan:
- Grace will start with connection-level traces and conntrack/conn-state checks.
- We'll check DNS resolution history and edge selection for the failing requests.
- I'll loop in Monica for communications and Vivek if we need exec approval for credits or expedited firewall changes.

Can we stand up a 30-minute bridge if we need to escalate? If yes, what window works for you in the next 90 minutes?

— Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Irwin <sam@suncrest-commerce.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — preliminary findings

Quick triage notes (high level):

What I validated so far (from customer PCAP + our egress telemetry):
- DNS: Suncrest resolved our edge hostname to a US-WEST address (redwood-edge-usw2-1.example.net -> 198.51.100.42) consistently in the failing traces. However, after traceroutes we saw asymmetric routing: traffic from Suncrest hits our peering, then is hairpinned through a transit hop back to a different colo before reaching the inference host. There are ~40-60ms extra RTTs and a higher packet retransmit rate on that path.

- NAT/Proxy: conntrack samples show ports near exhaustion on our proxy/NAT pool in the affected AZ during the spike window. When conntrack entries are reclaimed we see TCP RSTs and incomplete TLS handshakes (this explains the 5xx/connection reset pattern). Snapshot attached (conntrack-snapshot.txt).

- Firewall/Proxy health/idle timeouts: our proxy was recycling long-lived upstream connections due to an aggressive idle timeout combined with a reachability flapping induced by the asymmetric path. That causes re-establishment storms which amplify conntrack pressure.

Trace snippet (simplified):
> 08:12:17.123 Suncrest -> redwood-edge-usw2-1.example.net (SYN)
> 08:12:17.187 transit-hop-2 -> redwood-host-23 (SYN, retransmit)
> 08:12:17.310 redwood-proxy -> Suncrest (RST)

Recommended immediate mitigations (can be done in parallel):
1) Increase conntrack timeout and expand ephemeral port/NAT pool on the affected proxy (SRE change, low risk, ETA 30-90m).
2) Add a temporary route pin on Suncrest's peering to prefer direct egress to our west edge (customer change) — reduces hairpinning (ETA customer + network team coordination: 2-4 hrs).
3) Lower DNS TTL for the edge hostname to 30s so any cached/stale addresses expire faster (change on our DNS and advise Suncrest to flush).
4) Short-term: enable a regional fallback host group (route to alternate west-edge) for the customer's traffic via routing policy so retries go to a healthier path (config change, ETA 1-2 hrs).

We can stabilize traffic with 1 + 4 within ~2 hours in the best case. The firewall/peering change will take longer and requires customer and carrier coordination.

Ask: Rishi / Monica — we need executive sign-off to offer a one-time SLA credit and to approve an expedited network change that touches our peering/firewall rules (this will require approvals from network and legal if it exceeds standard maintenance windows). Vivek — assigning to you given the potential customer impact and the need for a quick customer-facing decision.

I'll keep collecting conntrack and proxy metrics; attaching a short flowlog excerpt (flowlogs-sample.csv) and the conntrack snapshot.

— Grace
Senior SRE, Traffic Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Irwin <sam@suncrest-commerce.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike — action plan and exec ask

Team / Sam — summary and agreed next steps following today's triage: 

What happened: asymmetric peering + transient hairpin created extra RTTs and packet loss triggering proxy connection churn and conntrack exhaustion. That chain manifested as a 5xx spike and elevated p95 for Suncrest traffic.

Immediate actions we will take (owners & ETA):
- Grace / SRE: expand NAT/ephemeral pool and relax conntrack reclaim thresholds (ETA: 60–90 minutes).
- Network: deploy route pinning for Suncrest so peered traffic prefers the direct west-edge (customer & network coordination; ETA: 2–4 hours).
- Platform: enable regional fallback host group for Suncrest so retries go to alternate healthy edge (ETA: 60–120 minutes).
- DNS: reduce edge TTL and coordinate flush for Suncrest's resolvers (ETA: 1–2 hours).

Customer-facing commitments:
- Immediate stabilization target: reduce 5xx to <1% and restore p95 to <350ms for affected traffic within 2 hours of completing the SRE mitigation.
- We'll keep you updated every 30 minutes while changes are in progress.

Executive ask / approval: 
- Monica / Vivek: request approval to offer Suncrest a pro-rated SLA credit for the affected interval and to authorize an expedited firewall/peering change outside the normal maintenance window if network timeline pushes beyond 2 hours.

Bridge: I'll schedule a 30-minute bridge if we need live coordination — proposed link: https://zoom.us/j/9999999990?pwd=incident-bridge (see Drive folder for artifacts).

Attachments: trace-20261113-0815.pcap, conntrack-snapshot.txt, flowlogs-sample.csv

Sam — thanks for the quick artifacts. Grace and our network on-call will proceed with the mitigations and I'll send status updates. If you want the bridge now, let me know and we will start it.

— Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
